report: Quiet day for orders, good day for the one position. The trader placed no new orders. It kept holding Infineon, six shares bought at 50.90 euros. The reasons: JP Morgan put a Buy rating on it today, and the strong guidance for next year still stands. Infineon closed at 52.12, up from 49.05 yesterday. That is now 2.4 percent above our entry. The position has 9 trading days left, with an exit by November 24. The input does not show a stop level, so I cannot say how far away it is. In the wider market, US inflation came in hot. That raised bets on rate hikes and firmed the dollar. US stocks fell on an Nvidia slide, but European indices rose. Oil, gold and copper all rose overnight. None of them came with a company-specific trigger big enough to beat our costs, so those themes stayed flat. There were no fills today and no rejected orders. Custody cost was a tenth of a cent. Reconcile is consistent and there are no warnings. The day made 18.42 euros, plus 1.9 percent. The account stands at 1004.85 euros, up about half a percent in total. Be careful with this. One stock rising for one day is mostly market mood and luck. It does not prove the trade idea was right. One small oddity: the previous handoff was already dated today.
questions: The open position has no stop level in today's input. Should every position carry an explicit stop in the handoff and day report, and what should it be for Infineon?
The trader keeps citing the BofA downgrade of three European chip stocks without knowing the names. Should an unconfirmed report like that count for anything until a primary source names the stocks?

The previous handoff was already dated 2026-11-11, the same day as this review. Did the trader or reviewer run twice today, and could that cause decisions to use a handoff that is out of step with the day?
